{{Quote|This is Commander Gobee to Flight Leader Kurt&mdash;''"<br />"''Kurt here. Yes, Commander?|Flight Leader Kurt, during the Battle of Iziz|audio=Kurt1-TOTJ.flac|<ref name="totj" />}}
'''Kurt''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] native to the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] Territories [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]. A member of the [[Beast Riders]] of Onderon's wilderness, Kurt was the [[Flight leader/Legends|flight leader]] of several [[Squadron/Legends|squads]], or "[[Fighter wing/Legends|wings]]," of [[drexl]]-mounted warriors in the [[Beast Rider army]].

Under the [[Commander/Legends|command]] of the superior officer [[Gobee]], Kurt saw action during the [[Battle of Iziz|final battle]] of Onderon's [[Beast Wars|centuries-long civil conflict]], between his Beast Rider kin and the [[City/Legends|city]]-dwellers of [[Iziz/Legends|Iziz]], Onderon's only civilized metropolis. He assisted Gobee by eliminating Iziz's [[Iziz defense tower|perimeter defenses]], and then suppressing the [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] bombardment originating from the rooftop of the [[Iziz Royal Palace]]. Kurt's actions led to the capture of the city as well as the subsequent defeat of the Iziz forces.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Haul your Beast Riders off the eastern wall and swing 'em around to the Palace!|Commander Gobee, to Flight Leader Kurt|audio=Kurt2-TOTJ.flac|<ref name="totj" />}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Kurt was a [[Beast Riders|Beast Rider]] from the wilderness of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], and by the year [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], he achieved the rank of [[Flight leader/Legends|flight leader]] in the [[Beast Rider army]]. As a flight leader, Kurt commanded several [[Squadron/Legends|squads]], or "[[Fighter wing/Legends|wings]]," of [[drexl]]-riding warriors. He himself was the subordinate of [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Gobee]].<ref name="totj" />

In the year 4,000 BBY, the [[Beast Wars|centuries-long conflict]] that plagued Kurt's [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] between his beast-riding people and the citizens of [[Iziz/Legends|Iziz]], Onderon's only [[City/Legends|city]], was finally drawing to a close. The Beast Riders had risen up against the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]-worshiping city-dwellers, who were led by the [[Sith sorcerer|sorceress]]-[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Amanoa]], whose own power stemmed from the memory of the [[Death/Legends|deceased]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Freedon Nadd]]. Refusing to be enslaved by the power of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], Kurt and his fellow Beast Riders united under the banner of [[Beast-Lord]] [[Modon Kira]]. The result was the largest host of warriors ever assembled against Iziz, gathered together with the intention of freeing the city from the oppression of the dark side.<ref name="totj" />

Early in [[Battle of Iziz|the battle]], Kurt's forces successfully eliminated the [[Iziz defense tower|defensive towers]] that lined Iziz's northern wall, allowing the ground [[Troop/Legends|troops]], mounted on wild [[boma]]-beasts, to enter the city unhindered. Kurt then led his riders in an attack against the eastern wall, as he had done successfully against the north side. However, Commander Gobee, who had dismounted his flying beast to lead the ground forces into the city, was pinned down with his troops at the feet of the [[Iziz Royal Palace]] by heavy enemy fire. With no other options, Gobee [[Comlink/Legends|commed]] Kurt and ordered his squad to discontinue their assault on the east wall, and bombard the palace roof with counterfire. Kurt immediately obliged, and succeeded in eliminating the rooftop [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]]. This allowed the Beast Riders to finally converge upon the citadel from all sides as Kurt continued to lend supporting fire to his planetside counterparts.<ref name="totj" />

After intense fighting, the battle and war were subsequently won by the Beast Riders, who managed to defeat the city-dwellers with assistance from several [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. In the wake of the fighting, those same Knights remained on Onderon, and further assisted in facilitating a peaceful coexistence between the city-dwellers and Kurt's Beast Rider kin.<ref name="totj" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Somebody lay some suppressing fire along that rooftop! I got ground troops taking heavy fire up there!''"<br />"''Affirmative! We're on our way!|Kurt, acknowledging Gobee's call for help|audio=Kurt3-TOTJ.flac|<ref name="totj" />}}
Flight leader Kurt was a solid military commander. A testament to his valor, Kurt led by example, leading the charge against enemies from the front lines of battle. As a subordinate of Commander Gobee, Kurt was extremely loyal and obedient, carrying out the senior officer's orders without question. Gobee trusted Kurt among his flight leaders to get the job done fast and efficiently.<ref name="totj" />

As a ranking officer in the Beast Rider army, Kurt was proficient with flying tamed drexl-beasts. While riding his beast, Kurt was able to redirect his efforts quickly and suddenly, often performing strafing runs and lending supporting fire to beleaguered ground troops from above. Kurt was also adept at firing the various ranged weapons while riding his beast, as most of his ilk were.<ref name="totj" />

==Behind the scenes==
The character of Kurt first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|audio dramatization]] of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon|''Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon'']] comic, written by [[John Whitman]] and based off the original script by author [[Tom Veitch]]. Kurt only has two short lines in the audio drama, and does not appear by name in the comic version of ''The Beast Wars of Onderon'' at all.

Furthermore, the actor who voiced Kurt's character was never credited alongside the other voice actors of the ''Tales of the Jedi'' audio, and the spelling of his name has never been [[canon]]ically printed anywhere. Thus, this article spells the name as is given that it is the most common spelling of the name in real life.
